ashes.description: A low-value residue item associated with spent fires and other firemaking output.
ashes.acquisition: The export links ashes to Firemaking economy data, but it does not expose the exact production step, so this remains a conservative fire-related byproduct entry.
ashes.uses: No major downstream crafting use is exported, so it mainly functions as a minor economy item.

boar_tusk.description: A boar tusk kept as one of the first animal-specific trophy drops in the starter combat loop.
boar_tusk.acquisition: Drops from Boar in Main Overworld.
boar_tusk.uses: Turn in 4 boar tusks with 2 wolf fangs to Tanner Rusk for Hides of the Frontier.

coins.description: Standard currency used across shop, trade, and value calculations.
coins.acquisition: The export does not expose a single primary source, so treat coins as general-purpose currency earned through broader gameplay systems.
coins.uses: Used to buy items from merchants and to represent value across the project economy.

feathers_bundle.description: A bundled feather resource used to finish headless arrow recipes in Fletching.
feathers_bundle.acquisition: Sold by the Fletching Supplier in the exported fletching economy tables.
feathers_bundle.uses: Combined with shafts across each wood tier to produce headless arrows for later arrow assembly.

goblin_club.description: A rough goblin club recovered as low-tier camp loot rather than player-ready equipment.
goblin_club.acquisition: Drops from Goblin Grunt in Main Overworld.
goblin_club.uses: No recipe or shop path is exported for it, so it mainly marks the jump from critter drops into roaming goblin encounters.

guard_crest.description: A guard crest taken as a recognizable patrol drop with more identity than the starter animal trophies.
guard_crest.acquisition: Drops from Guard in Main Overworld.
guard_crest.uses: No crafting or merchant path is exported for it, so it mainly serves as higher-tier patrol loot and named-faction flavor.

guard_spear.description: A guard spear recovered as loot rather than exported player equipment.
guard_spear.acquisition: Drops from Guard in Main Overworld.
guard_spear.uses: No equipment, recipe, or merchant path is exported for it yet, so it currently reads as higher-tier guard loot with presentation value more than utility.

hammer.description: A core workshop tool used throughout smithing and metal assembly recipes.
hammer.acquisition: Sold by Borin Ironvein through the exported smithing merchant tables in Main Overworld.
hammer.uses: Required for many smithing tasks and it also appears as a trade item in the smithing economy.

knife.description: A cutting tool used across fletching and simple crafting workflows.
knife.acquisition: Stocked by general stores in Main Overworld, with the exported default stock listing ten at a time.
knife.uses: Used to shape logs and related materials in fletching workflows, and it also appears in the fletching economy tables.

rat_tail.description: A rat tail kept as a disposable proof-of-kill drop from the very bottom of the combat ladder.
rat_tail.acquisition: Drops from Rat in Main Overworld.
rat_tail.uses: No recipe or merchant path is exported for it, so it mainly serves as low-value starter loot and encounter flavor.

soft_clay.description: A worked clay resource kept as a conservative crafting-material entry.
soft_clay.acquisition: Mainly produced through Crafting at level 1 at a water using Clay x1.
soft_clay.uses: Used in Crafting recipes that produce Imprinted Amulet Mould, Imprinted Ring Mould, Imprinted Tiara Mould.

tinderbox.description: A basic firemaking tool used to ignite logs.
tinderbox.acquisition: Stocked by general stores in Main Overworld through the exported firemaking and general-store economy data.
tinderbox.uses: Used to light logs for Firemaking.

wolf_fang.description: A wolf fang kept as a more dangerous animal trophy from the far-out starter-region encounter bands.
wolf_fang.acquisition: Drops from Wolf in Main Overworld.
wolf_fang.uses: Turn in 2 wolf fangs with 4 boar tusks to Tanner Rusk for Hides of the Frontier.
